children: By George Glover, Ty Roush, and Mariapaula Gonzalez

Stocks traded mixed Thursday as the artificial-intelligence selloff cooled after Nvidia's CEO said in a published report that CoreWeave won't need a backstop from the chip maker, helping ease some investor jitters.
Still, AI-related stocks tumbled. Advanced Micro Devices, Coherent, Corning, Intel, Lumentum, Marvell, and Sandisk all dropped on the continuing tech selloff.

Meanwhile, software stocks appeared to buck the tech selloff trend. Salesforce advanced 4.2%, Workday gained 4.7%, and Atlassian rose 3.1%. ServiceNow gained 4.8%, likely driven by two price target hikes, updates to its secure software for autonomous AI agents, and the announcement that it wouldn't acquire startup Decagon.

International Paper gained 7.3% and was the top performer in the S&P 500 following reports that private-equity firms Lone Star and Atlas Holdings were exploring multi-billion dollar buyout offers for the company's European packaging business.

Dell Technologies declined 8.4% and was the worst performer in the S&P 500. The company, along with Hewlett Packard Enterprise and NetApp, received a downgrade from Barclays the day on concerns that AI inflection has yet to drive significant revenue growth. HPE dropped 6.7%, while NetApp fell 3.4%.
CoreWeave fell 2.9% as worries about the cloud-computing company's debt mounted. Shares plummeted 15% on Wednesday as the yield on CoreWeave's 9.625% notes, due in 2032, surged.
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing fell 2.9% after the Taiwanese chip manufacturer's strong third-quarter earnings failed to lift the gloom engulfing the AI trade.
Apple rose 0.3%. The iPhone maker's total market capitalization topped $5 trillion for the first time ever on Wednesday, with shares benefiting from Apple spending much less on AI than its peers.
Penske Automotive advanced 8.5% after the car retailer announced it would be taken private after entering a merger agreement with Penske Corp. and Japanese trading firm Mitsui & Co.
Charles Schwab dropped 2.4%. The brokerage reported third-quarter earnings and revenue that exceeded consensus estimates.

Bloom Energy dropped 4.4% as energy stocks tied to the AI data-center buildout took a hit. Plug Power fell 0.3%, GE Vernova declined 2.9%, while Constellation Energy and Vistra fell 2.3% and 0.5%, respectively.
FMC plunged 31% after the crop chemical maker issued guidance for third-quarter earnings that fell well below Wall Street's consensus.
Rocket Lab slumped 11% after the company delayed the launch of its Neutron reusable rocket until next year, citing an issue with the manufacturing process.
